content:
devon: noticed elevated token p99 tails on apac1 dedicated racks. packet retransmits and 'Fragmentation needed and DF set' in dmesg.
sophia: any tcpdump evidence?
devon: saw IPIP payloads at ~1280B being dropped on some paths (overlay -> 1500 MTU).
matt: likely PMTU blackhole due to SR-IOV VF mtu vs overlay mismatch after kernel DF enforcement on proxies.
aj: is shared pool affected?
devon: mostly dedicated slices pinned to those racks; shared uses a different egress that clamps MSS.
sophia: mitigation options?
matt: short: MSS clamp on LB (NET-428). quick: enable net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 via daemonset (helps new connects).
lina: probing won't fix long-lived streams fully.
devon: propose: 1) apply daemonset canary (20%) now; 2) open NET ticket for MSS clamp + off-peak LB restart; 3) carve out egress for hottest tenants if needed (estimate ~$200/day per tenant); 4) long-term MTU harmonization and PMTU alerts.
aj: I'll own daemonset. using `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` and persisting in /etc/sysctl.d/99-mtu.conf.
matt: opened NET-428: add MSS clamp rule and schedule rolling restart at 23:00 local. link: https://net.company/NET-428
infra-bot: alert: apac1-edge-proxy-03 if_in_errors spike 2025-08-20T10:05:12Z
aj: canary applied to apac1 (pods 2/2). monitoring p99 and retransmit counters.
sophia: add alert for ICMP frag > 5/min per node and p99 token latency > 250ms for dedicated pools.
devon: affected tenants: t-15012, t-15099. t-15099 is top offender (~70%). product ok to cover short carveout costs up to $1k/day if we must.
aj: canary results: p99 down from ~480ms -> 140ms on canary hosts. rolling to rest.
lina: good. add runbook step: check dmesg for 'Fragmentation needed and DF set' pre-scale.
devon: updating incident doc and follow-ups for MTU monitoring. thanks all :thumbsup:
